verdict: Starbucks' turnaround gained ground — global comparable sales rose 6.2%, revenue grew 9% to $9.5B, and profit rose 33% to $511M as last year's heavy restructuring charges faded.

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP)
kpis.note: vs $0.34 a year ago; non-GAAP EPS was $0.50

segments.name: North America
segments.note: Coffeehouses in the U.S. and Canada — comparable store sales rose 7.1%, on more transactions (+4.4%) and bigger tickets (+2.6%).

segments.name: International
segments.note: Coffeehouses outside North America — licensed stores, currency tailwinds and 2.6% comparable sales growth; China comps rose 0.5%.

segments.name: Channel Development
segments.note: Packaged coffee and ready-to-drink drinks sold in grocery and convenience stores — growth came from the Global Coffee Alliance.

segments.name: Corporate & other
segments.note: Small leftover businesses and unallocated items.

opex.name: Depreciation & amortization
opex.note: Wear and tear on coffeehouses, roasteries and equipment — down 13% YoY, mostly because China store assets were classified as held for sale and stopped being depreciated.

opex.name: Restructuring & impairments
opex.note: Store closures and write-downs under 'Back to Starbucks' — down from $116M a year ago.

takeaways.title: The stores are turning
takeaways.text: Global comparable store sales rose 6.2% — more transactions (+3.8%) and bigger tickets (+2.3%). North America comps rose 7.1%: the 'Back to Starbucks' plan is showing up where it matters, in the stores.

takeaways.title: Revenue growth, at last
takeaways.text: Revenue rose 9% to $9.5B. Channel Development jumped 39% on the Global Coffee Alliance, International rose 10%, and North America 7%. Starbucks raised its full-year guidance for comparable sales and non-GAAP EPS.

takeaways.title: Profit up — with quieter charges
takeaways.text: Net earnings rose 33% to $511M and the GAAP operating margin widened to 8.7%, helped by restructuring charges falling to $25M from $116M a year ago and by China stores no longer being depreciated. The tax rate jumped to 29.8% on China reorganization items.

oneTimers: Restructuring and impairment charges were $25M — store closures under 'Back to Starbucks' — versus $116M a year ago.

Starbucks classified its China retail operations as held for sale in Q1 FY26 (they moved into the Boyu Capital joint venture just after quarter-end), which stopped depreciation on those stores and lowered reported costs; the quarter's 29.8% tax rate included an $8M discrete charge tied to that classification.
otherDetail: $51M of income from equity investees and $37M of interest and other income, less $137M of interest expense.
footerNote: Reported operating income of $828M includes $51M of income from equity investees; this page shows that in Other income (the same treatment as the Q3/Q4 FY26 pages), so the operating-profit block reads $777M. Starbucks reports in tenths of millions — lines are rounded to whole millions and tie exactly. Essentially all of the $511M of net earnings is attributable to Starbucks (noncontrolling interests were about $0M).
